defects: The run-002 tabletop shows a broad room reflection, but it reads greener and more transparent than the photographed smoked-glass desk; floor and wall colors show through too strongly.
The front glass edge is still a thin dark line rather than the source photo and approved target’s clearly lit glass edge.
The room overview makes v061’s material and construction gain modest; it does not transform the room at the 330-inch view.
hard_fail_reasons: The source-character gate remains unmet: the smoked top is too transparent and green in the production room render.
The target’s continuous bright edge response is still not carried into the production three-quarter and detail views.
incumbent_comparison: In same-current-project run-004 versus run-002, v061 has the stronger constructed underframe and more readable broad glass reflection. Its candidate-local reflection probe is the key response: a controlled no-probe wrapper keeps the same geometry and effective materials but loses the room reflections. The v061 close views are better than v007, while its translucent green cast remains off target.
next_action_hypothesis: Set desk-v061 as the best current review candidate, keep desk-v007 in the production registry, and leave the approved r01 episode backlogged at its three-strategy limit. Move to room-shell trim. Revisit the desk only under a newly approved Visual Director target and a materially different source-conditioned strategy that controls tabletop opacity and edge reflection.

observations.art_direction_fit: The multipart standing desk now fits the contemporary room more deliberately than v007, though the green transmission tint makes the top too conspicuous.
observations.close_up_quality: The run-002 detail view shows separate columns, rail, saddles, feet and fittings; the glass edge still lacks the target’s brighter continuous highlight.
observations.gameplay_readability: The tabletop plane and paired support frame are more distinguishable than v007 in the room and three-quarter views, but the room-scale gain remains modest.
observations.geometric_detail: Twenty-two separate components preserve the paired telescoping columns, under-glass rail, collars, saddles, T-feet, levelers and fittings.
observations.material_realism: The matched effective StandardMaterial3D values are correct and the probe restores broad reflection; the 0.58 alpha and room-color transmission still make the glass too green and transparent.
observations.proportion: The validated v061 scene remains exactly 66 x 30 x 30 inches and fits the existing RoomDefinition placement.
observations.scale_fidelity: The desk retains the authoritative 66 x 30 x 30-inch visual envelope; no RoomDefinition center, orientation, navigation footprint or surface anchor changed.
observations.semantic_recognizability: The room-scale and close captures clearly read as a standing computer desk with a broad top and T-frame supports.
observations.silhouette_quality: Run-002 preserves a wide thin top, open knee space, two supports and perpendicular feet.
observations.source_resemblance: The shape and reflection character approach the photographed desk, but its near-black smoked surface is still greener and more see-through than the source.
observations.surface_variation: The probe reveals separation between glass, graphite and room reflections, but the green wall transmission and dark metal still compress the value hierarchy.
observations.technical_integration: Godot 4.7.2 imported and rendered the 22-mesh PackedScene through the production resolver with exact bounds and 50 active citizens.

close_inspection.evidence: Run-002 shows the model’s support construction clearly; the leading glass edge and tabletop material hierarchy still fall short of a finished source-faithful desk.

edge_treatment.evidence: The three-quarter and detail renders show a continuous thin edge, but its highlight stays too dark against the approved target.

hardware.evidence: The small mounts and fasteners exist but remain difficult to read against the dark support structure in the detail capture.

joins.evidence: The run-002 detail shows saddles and the continuous under-glass rail connecting the columns to the top.

manufacturing_detail.evidence: The close view distinguishes the paired column stages, overlap collars, rail, saddles and perpendicular feet.

material_response.evidence: The reflection probe adds broad room reflection, but transmitted green wall/floor values overwhelm the dark smoked-glass character.

surface_variation.evidence: The tabletop is distinct from the support, yet glass tint and graphite values still merge into a dark green-black palette.

thickness.evidence: The profile render retains a thin desktop with no oversized glass slab or silhouette break.

neutral_viewer_realism.evidence: In the matched production close captures, the glass is recognizably a desk top, but green wall and floor transmission keep it from reading as the near-black smoked glass in the source and approved target.

photo_character.evidence: The production render preserves the source silhouette and now has broad reflections, but the table is too transparent and green and the bright front glass edge remains weak.

visual_transfer_diagnosis.corrective_action: Keep v061 as best current review, retain v007 in production, preserve the three-attempt r01 backlog, and move to trim. A future desk episode needs a newly approved target and a materially different treatment of opacity and edge reflection.
lost_visual_information: The source and approved target present dark smoked glass with a clearer continuous edge highlight; run-002 transmits too much green wall and floor color.
The 330-inch room overview still gives only a modest screen-space gain over v007.
preserved_components: Exact 66 x 30 x 30-inch envelope and RoomDefinition-owned placement.
The 22-part desk construction: twin telescoping columns, under-glass rail, fittings, and perpendicular T-feet.
Godot-native glass, graphite, satin and rubber materials remain assigned to their intended mesh groups.
